maya: heads-up — saw a p99 tail jump after yesterday's kernel picker tweak (stable -> heuristic-v2). p99 from ~120ms -> ~185ms on short-chat workload. timeline: deploy @ 10:07 UTC then tail spike ~10:11. anyone else seeing this?

sam: saw it too. correlates with queue delay increasing. max_wait_ms set to 12, max_batch_tokens 8192 on that pool. qdelay p95 went +8ms, p99 +25ms.

priya: KV cache hit-rate dropped on that window from 98% -> 85%. looks like more cold/shard misses when kernel switches happen mid-request. trace snippet: `kv.hit_rate=0.85 kv.evictions=123`

toni: fwiw heuristic-v2 tends to re-evaluate kernel per microbatch when seq_len variance > 0.5x which causes short warmups. fallback path adds ~3-6ms/warmup on p99.

maya: interesting — so two hypotheses: (A) batching policy holding requests longer (qdelay) to assemble larger microbatches, (B) kernel churn causing extra startup latencies + KV thrash.

sam: quick mitigation we tested locally: lower max_wait_ms -> 6ms and cap max_batch_tokens to 4096. that cut p99 by ~30ms on a simulated short-chat trace. tradeoff: throughput dropped ~4% but p50/p95 improved.

priya: also try enabling `kv_prefetch=true` on the pool. prefetch reduces cold miss penalty when kernel switch happens. small config diff:
```json
{"max_wait_ms":6,"max_batch_tokens":4096,"kv_prefetch":true}
```

toni: alternative is forcing kernel_stable for <64 token generation. cheap heuristic: if request.seq_len_est <= 64 then pin kernel to fast-short which avoids recompile/handshake. reduces churn.

maya: do we have profiling traces that show kernel handshake costs? i captured a flame for 10:11 spike: `handshake_ms` buckets show 12ms spikes on p99. link: https://perf.internal/runs/2765432100/flare (will upload full traces)

sam: nice. also check dispatcher queue metrics — we saw microburst tails where one worker had >150ms head-of-line while others idle. might be uneven batching boundary alignment.

priya: metadata from logs: `seq_var=high shard=3 kernel_change=true kv_miss_bulk=true` — suggests simultaneous kernel_change + kv_miss. those amplify tail.

toni: suggestion for a short rollout: 1) set max_wait_ms=6 on the short-chat route, 2) enable kv_prefetch=true, 3) add kernel pin for seq<=64, 4) monitor p99 for 2h. if stable, widen to other pools.

maya: +1. i'll run a controlled canary on 5% traffic. can someone prepare the rollout PR and a perf runbook?

sam: i'll open PR with the config delta and a small load generator test.

priya: i'll attach KV hit-rate dashboards and alert thresholds (alert if hit_rate < 92% or p99 > 160ms).

deploy-bot: deploy queued by @sam for pool=short-chat-canvas, change-set=kv_prefetch+waitms-cap, rollout=canary(5%) at 10:42 UTC.

maya: thanks — after canary I'll post full profiles and decide on kernel-picker rollback vs config tweak. :thumbsup:

sam: FYI we'll also try a microbatch size sweep (128/256/512 tokens) to see where tail vs throughput sweet spot is. will share numbers in thread.

toni: if anyone needs quick script to parse traces, use `tools/trace-summarize --group-by=handshake_ms,queue_delay` (gives percentiles and event-correlation).

maya: perfect. keeping thread open while canary runs. ping me @maya if you see p99 > 180ms.
